title: Reverse Only Letters
description:
Given a string `s`, reverse the string according to the following rules:

- All characters that are not English letters remain in the same position.
- All English letters (lowercase `'a'-'z'` or uppercase `'A'-'Z'`) are reversed in place.

Return the resulting string.
constraints: s consists of characters with ASCII values in the range [33, 122].
hints: Place one pointer at the start of the string and another at the end, moving them toward each other.
Advance the left pointer until it points to an English letter, and move the right pointer backward until it also points to an English letter.
Swap the two letters and advance both pointers inward until they meet or cross.

examples.explanation: The letters 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd' are reversed to 'd', 'c', 'b', 'a', while '-' stays at index 2, giving "dc-ba".
All hyphens stay at their original positions while the English letters reverse to form "j-Ih-gfE-dCba".
Digits and punctuation ('1', '-', '=', '!') stay fixed while the letters reverse to yield "Qedo1ct-eeLg=ntse-T!".
